title: GTA VI’s Six-Hour Netflix Preview Reportedly Drove More Than 100,000 U.S. Sign-Ups
description: GTA VI’s six-hour Netflix-exclusive Extended Look reportedly drove more than 100,000 U.S. sign-ups, making it one of Netflix’s biggest subscriber events of 2026.
body:
**Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look reportedly drove more than 100,000 new Netflix sign-ups in the United States during its six-hour exclusivity window on August 27.**

According to Ampere Analysis data reported on September 10, the GTA VI presentation produced Netflix’s third-highest U.S. subscriber acquisition peak of 2026.

The result is another measure of just how far GTA VI has moved beyond a conventional game marketing cycle — and it may give Netflix and other streaming platforms a reason to pursue more major gaming reveals.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Grand Theft Auto VI artwork featuring Jason and Lucia on a Vice City beach.

contentBlocks.text: Rockstar premiered **Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look** on Netflix on August 27 with a six-hour exclusivity window before the 27-minute presentation became available elsewhere. According to Ampere Analysis data reported on September 10, that window drove **more than 100,000 new U.S. Netflix sign-ups** on launch day.
contentBlocks.heading: Six hours were enough to move Netflix subscriptions

contentBlocks.text: Ampere says the GTA VI event became **Netflix’s third-highest U.S. subscriber acquisition peak of 2026**. Only the final installment of *Stranger Things* and the Ronda Rousey vs. Gina Carano MMA event generated larger sign-up spikes during the measured period.
contentBlocks.heading: One of Netflix’s biggest acquisition spikes of 2026

contentBlocks.text: The effect was not limited to new accounts. Ampere’s PlumResearch data found that **more than 5% of U.S. Netflix users who had not watched the service during the previous 30 days returned and watched the GTA VI presentation before anything else**. The reported reactivation rate was higher than that of any series or film during the measured period.
contentBlocks.heading: Inactive subscribers came back for GTA VI too

contentBlocks.text: The subscriber data follows an enormous viewing debut for Rockstar’s presentation. Netflix reported **31.1 million views** for *Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look* between August 27 and August 30, placing it at No. 1 among English-language films for the week and at No. 1 in 87 of the 93 countries tracked by the service.
contentBlocks.heading: The Extended Look was already a huge viewing event

contentBlocks.text: The result suggests Netflix does not need to publish a AAA game itself to benefit from the attention around one. Major reveals, trailers and developer showcases can function as streaming events, giving platforms a way to compete for gaming audiences through video rather than direct game development.
contentBlocks.heading: Netflix may have found another route into gaming

contentBlocks.text: What makes the figure especially striking is that the exclusivity was brief. Viewers knew the presentation would become freely available after only six hours, yet Ampere’s estimate suggests more than 100,000 people in the U.S. still chose to subscribe during the launch window rather than wait.
contentBlocks.heading: A six-hour window mattered because viewers could simply wait

contentBlocks.text: Rockstar’s next Grand Theft Auto is increasingly behaving like a broader entertainment event before release. Its trailers and showcases dominate online attention, and the new Netflix data suggests that attention can translate into measurable subscriber behavior for companies outside the games business.
contentBlocks.heading: GTA VI is becoming an event beyond gaming

contentBlocks.text: **Grand Theft Auto VI launches November 19, 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.** Rockstar currently lists those two platforms for launch.
contentBlocks.heading: Grand Theft Auto VI launches November 19
